Prevention: Use clean certified seed from agro-shops
Soak seeds in a bowl of hot water at 50°C for 25 minutes (Mix half cold and half boiling water)
Bury 40cm deep all plant residues from the previous crop and weeds during land preparation.
Space plants far enough to allow for good air movement between plants (such as 1 x 1 m)
Stake plants to keep leaves and fruit from contacting the soil and mulch with spear grass to reduce "soil splash" onto the plants
Irrigate plants in the morning if you see any signs of infection during the dry season.
Watering in the evening would make early blight spread fast.
Crop rotation for 3-4 growing seasons with maize or beans but not potato, pepper or eggplant
Monitoring: Most likely symptoms will appear in dump growing conditions
Symptoms appear after fruit set, starting on lower leaves as tiny dark brown spots
Distinct brown to back spots on leaves, stems and fruits with concentric circles
On green fruits a spot appears at a point where fruit attaches the stalk
When you see 1-2 lower leaves with infection on at least 3-5 plants per 5m 2 , consider direct control especially during rain.
Direct Control: Prevention is the most powerful measure.
Direct control is difficult and often too late
Remove diseased leaves or fruits from the plant at earliest signs and bury (1m deep) or burn as this will reduce further spread
